title: What if… cytokinin meets auxin in developing roots? The story behind root ring formation
content: Auxin–cytokinin antagonism is a core regulatory principle in plant development. In the root apical meristem, auxin maxima and gradients contribute to patterning and help maintain meristematic growth, whereas cytokinin (CK) promotes the transition to differentiation and limits meristem size (Schaller et al. 2015). Through reciprocal inhibition and spatial separation of their signaling outputs, auxin and cytokinin function within sharp developmental boundaries. Root development involves more than elongation: in addition to primary growth in length, roots must also thicken through secondary growth. This thickening is driven by lateral meristems, which build stronger, more efficient transport tissues. A ring of dividing cells called the vascular cambium produces secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward, whereas the cork cambium (phellogen) forms the protective periderm (Evert 2006).
